answer: One defence: every new identity must forge a proof of costly memory-hard work before it can submit, whose output seeds the next round, so ten thousand clones cost ten thousand real machine-hours. Weight comes from peer-attested work, not identity count: ungraded submissions sit pending and earn nothing. It grinds a sybil farm like a glacier grinds stone, by slow attrition. Under that pressure cheap duplicates never reach the trusted set, while verified labour compresses into something solid and clear, an opal of proven work rather than raw count. That marginal-cost asymmetry is the filter.
